knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A sign does not stop a person walking in. A barrier is placed first, with the sign at both ends.
A cable across a walkway creates a trip hazard, and on a wet floor it adds to the slip risk.
The drying time is part of the sequence, and the area stays closed until it has passed.

practicalCriteria: Checks the route and floor condition and records any defect before starting
Places a barrier and then a sign at both ends of a wet section
Parks equipment off the route and secures a cable across it
Reports a simulated defect to the supervisor and keeps the area closed
passRule: Knowledge checks are a reading check only and are not verified practical competence. Assessor must observe every practical criterion; any failure requires remediation and reassessment.
stopWorkCriteria: A wet section is left open in a traffic route with no barrier
A route with a defect is used without a report
